notes:
Yuan Shao, warlord state of the four northern provinces 191-207. 5 pages opened (Yuan Shao, End of the Han dynasty, Yuan Tan, Gao Gan, Gongsun Zan), the 3-12-shape budget; the state has no Cliopatria row.
Settled: Ji 191; Qing 193 (Yuan Tan); Beihai 196; You after Yijing in April-May 199; the four provinces by 199; Ye and Bing 204; Nanpi and Qing 205; heirs eliminated 207.
Unsettled: (1) Bing Province's date of taking is not on any opened page (199 at confidence 1); (2) 203 (Gao Gan page) against 204 (End of the Han) for Gao Gan's surrender; (3) Tian Kai driven out of Qing in 193 (Yuan Shao page) against only a truce in 193 (Yuan Tan page); (4) who held You Province 204-207 (Yuan Xi?) is not on the pages, the 204 and 205-206 keyframes are confidence 1; (5) provinces are drawn as modern provinces; (6) Yuan Shao died on 28 June 202 (infobox): no land moved, the sons split Ye (Yuan Shang) and Pingyuan (Yuan Tan); no ledger event carries it because the schema has no event type for a succession.
Counterparts: han-dynasty and cao-cao exist; gongsun-zan is written by this batch. Liaodong's Gongsun Du (gongsun-liaodong exists) was outside Yuan's lands. Not mapped: Yuan Shu (south of the Huai from 191), Zhang Yan's Heishan men.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): (1) Ji Province is southern Hebei only for 191-198 (and after, minus the Heishan's circle): the Yuan Shao page calls Ji 'present day southern Hebei' and You '(present day northern Hebei)'. K0-K2, /ledger/0 and the 204 loss are Hebei minus the Baoding 100 km circle (gongsun-zan's Yijing), the northern arcs of You (Zhangjiakou, Chengde, Tangshan, Qinhuangdao, Langfang; an approximation, confidence 1, no page gives the Ji-You frontier) and the Taihang circle of the yellow-turbans dossier (Shijiazhuang 120 km, 185-205). You (Beijing, Tianjin and northern Hebei, 'covering present-day northern Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin and Liaoning' on the End of the Han page) is added only at 199 (/ledger/5). Bing is Shanxi minus the Taihang circle. Checked with the gazetteer: no cell shared with the yellow-turbans shape, none with gongsun-zan except in 199, the year Yijing falls. (2) The 193 Qing gain keeps gongsun-zan as counterpart; gongsun-zan has no matching loss (the Gongsun Zan page has Tian Kai only as Inspector of Qing 'appointed', undated) and was not touched (thin): written into /ledger/2 as a mirror exception. gongsun-zan's You stops at Baoding 100 km, so the northern arcs cut out here are drawn for nobody in 193-198 until a gap-filler extends it. (3) Bing: the Gao Gan page, reopened, gives 'about seven years' to 206 (so about 199) and 'surrender to Cao Cao in 203'; no appointer; /ledger/4 stays at confidence 1. (4) You Province 204-207: the Yuan Shao page says only that Yuan Xi 'moved to You Province after Yuan Shao's death' (undated); the Yuan Xi page was not opened (five-page budget).
